Risk Description:
Market risk is the potential
impact to capital as a
result of values of assets
and liabilities or revenues
adversely affected by
changes in market
conditions or market
movements. It arises from
movements in market
prices particularly changes
in interest rates, foreign
currency exchange rates,
fixed rate securities and
equity prices which we are
exposed to.
Assessment:
• Market KRIs, interest
rates risk balance sheet,
interest rates maturity
analysis from a time
bucket perspective,
mark to market fixed
income securities
portfolios, are regularly
reported and reviewed at
ALCO & BARC.
Treasury department
manages this risk on a daily
basis using some of the
above techniques in addition
to ensuring interest rates in
the banking book are well
controlled.
Distinct market risk
exposures for which specific
limits in place are:
Interest rate risk.
Foreign exchange risk.
Price risk.
Mitigation:
Market risk appetite and KRIs are monitored
and reported against the actual market risk
exposures to ensure they are within the
approved appetite.
The matching and controlled mismatching
of the maturities and interest and foreign
exchange rates of assets and liabilities is
fundamental to the management of the
Group’s market risk though it is unusual to
completely be matched due to the nature of
business terms & types of products offered.
The Group also ensures that the single
currency and overall market risk exposures
are within the internal and regulatory position
limits of maximum 10% of its core capital.
Finally, the Group ensures fixed income
securities portfolios operate within the
approved appetites / limits.
